title: Give every agent a tool budget before it starts
excerpt: Unlimited tool calls look powerful in demos and expensive in production—here is how to set a budget that still ships work.
angles: Define max tool calls, wall-clock, and spend before the first act
Separate cheap reads from expensive writes
Degrade gracefully when the budget is hit instead of looping forever
try_this: Pick one live agent run and add hard caps: N tool calls, M seconds, $X. Log when each cap is hit.

title: Human gates that protect without freezing the pipeline
excerpt: Approval steps should catch irreversible writes—not every intermediate draft. Design gates that keep throughput.
angles: Gate on irreversible side effects, not on thinking
Batch approvals with a clear yes/no/revise contract
Timeouts and escalation paths beat silent waits
try_this: List your agent’s side effects. Mark which ones need a human. Remove gates from everything else.

title: Treat the context window like working memory, not a junk drawer
excerpt: Stuffing every ticket into the prompt feels thorough until the model loses the goal. Curate what stays in frame.
angles: Keep the goal and success criteria pinned at the top
Summarize history; keep raw sources behind tools
Evict stale tool noise on purpose
try_this: For one agent, write a 5-line context policy: always keep, summarize, fetch on demand, never include.

title: Make agent writes idempotent or do not let them write
excerpt: Retries are normal. Duplicate CRM notes and double emails are not. Design writes so a second attempt is safe.
angles: Use idempotency keys on every external write
Prefer upsert over create-blind
Record write receipts in the trace before claiming success
try_this: Add an idempotency key to one write path and replay the same run twice. Confirm a single external effect.

title: Retrieve first, then reason—not the other way around
excerpt: Models invent confidently when evidence is missing. Force a retrieve step before claims that need facts.
angles: Separate “what we know” from “what we infer”
Fail closed when retrieval returns nothing material
Cite sources in the artifact, not only in the trace
try_this: Add a hard rule: no numeric claim without a retrieved source id attached in the draft.

title: Give your agent an SLA, not vibes about “fast enough”
excerpt: Users forgive a slower answer less than a silent hang. Name the latency budget and design for it.
angles: Publish p50/p95 targets per job type
Parallelize independent tool calls
Return a partial useful result when time is nearly gone
try_this: Measure wall-clock for 20 recent runs. Set a p95 target and add a soft stop at 80% of that budget.

title: Schemas between agents beat polite natural language
excerpt: Handoffs fail when specialists improvise structure. Contract the payload so the next step can trust it.
angles: Define required fields and types for every handoff
Validate on receive; reject incomplete packets early
Version the schema when the job changes
try_this: Write a JSON schema for one agent-to-agent handoff and validate it in the orchestrator before continuing.

title: Version prompts like code, observe them like products
excerpt: Prompt drift is a silent regression. Treat prompt text as a deployed artifact with owners and diffs.
angles: Store prompt templates with version ids in the trace
A/B only with outcome metrics, not taste tests alone
Rollback prompts as easily as you rollback code
try_this: Put today’s system prompt in git with a version tag and log that tag on every run.

title: Plan for tools that lie, time out, or return empty
excerpt: Happy-path agents die in production. Explicit fallbacks turn flaky APIs into recoverable runs.
angles: Classify tool errors: retry, degrade, escalate, abort
Never invent data to paper over an empty response
Surface the degraded path in the user-facing result
try_this: Chaos-test one tool: force timeout and empty payload. Confirm the agent chooses a documented fallback.

title: Pick one success metric per agent job
excerpt: Dashboards grow; clarity shrinks. One primary outcome metric keeps the loop honest.
angles: Define done before you define tools
Secondary metrics explain; they do not redefine success
Review weekly: did the metric predict user value?
try_this: Write one sentence: “This agent succeeds when ___.” Put it at the top of the run config.

title: Chunk for the question, not for the embedding model’s comfort
excerpt: Bad retrieval is usually a chunking problem wearing a model costume. Align chunks to how people ask.
angles: Prefer semantic units (procedure, FAQ, policy) over fixed token slices
Keep enough surrounding context to answer without neighbors
Evaluate retrieval with real user questions, not synthetic trivia
try_this: Take 10 failed answers. For each, check whether the right chunk was retrieved before blaming the LLM.

title: Track cost per successful outcome, not cost per token
excerpt: Cheap tokens that fail still burn money. Price the finished job users care about.
angles: Attribute spend to completed, aborted, and retried runs
Compare model tiers on outcome rate, not sticker price
Cut steps that do not move the success metric
try_this: For last week’s runs, compute $ per successful outcome. Cut the most expensive non-contributing step.

title: Long-term memory needs an expiry date
excerpt: Agents that remember forever eventually remember the wrong thing. TTL and provenance beat infinite recall.
angles: Tag memories with source, confidence, and expiry
Prefer re-fetching volatile facts over caching them
Let users correct or delete what the agent stored
try_this: Add TTL + source fields to one memory write path. Purge anything past expiry on read.

title: Grow your eval set from real failures, not imagined ones
excerpt: Synthetic evals miss the messy cases production invents. Promote incidents into lasting tests.
angles: Every production miss becomes a fixture within a week
Keep fixtures small and labeled by failure mode
Re-run the suite before every prompt or tool change
try_this: Take the last three user complaints. Turn each into a scored eval case with a clear pass condition.

title: Stream progress so users trust the wait
excerpt: A blank spinner feels broken. Show plan, acts, and checks as they happen without dumping raw chain-of-thought.
angles: Expose phase labels users understand
Hide tool secrets; show outcomes
Allow cancel mid-run with a clean stop
try_this: Add three user-visible phases to one agent UI: planning, gathering, drafting. Measure abandon rate.

title: Write agent policy as code, not as a hope in the prompt
excerpt: “Be careful with PII” in a system prompt is not a control. Enforce policy where tools execute.
angles: Put allow/deny lists in the tool layer
Redact before logs leave the boundary
Fail closed on ambiguous permission
try_this: Move one safety rule out of the prompt and into a tool-side check that cannot be talked around.

title: Route models by job shape, not by brand loyalty
excerpt: One frontier model for every step is simple and often wasteful. Match model class to task class.
angles: Classify steps: extract, plan, write, judge
Use small models for structured extraction
Reserve large models for ambiguous reasoning
try_this: Split one pipeline into extract vs write. Benchmark quality and cost with a smaller model on extract.

title: Prefer structured outputs when the next step is a machine
excerpt: Prose is for people. Schemas are for the next tool call. Choose the shape that matches the consumer.
angles: Ask for JSON/schema when another system will consume it
Validate before acting
Keep a human-readable summary as a separate field
try_this: Change one agent handoff from free text to a validated object. Count parse failures for a week.

title: Replay yesterday’s traces before you change today’s prompt
excerpt: Guessing how a prompt change will behave is optional. Replaying recorded traces is not.
angles: Store enough of the run to re-score offline
Diff outcomes across prompt versions
Block deploys when replay regressions spike
try_this: Save 25 recent traces. Re-score them against your success metric after the next prompt edit.

title: Every production agent needs a named owner
excerpt: Orphan agents rot. Ownership means alerts, evals, and the right to turn the thing off.
angles: Assign an on-call for failures and cost spikes
Document kill switches
Review weekly: still worth running?
try_this: Add OWNER and KILL_SWITCH fields to the agent config. Page the owner on success-rate drops.

title: AI features need data contracts too
excerpt: Model quality cannot fix silent schema drift upstream. Contract the inputs your agent depends on.
angles: Version the fields tools expect
Alert when required columns go null
Refuse to run when the contract breaks
try_this: Write a one-page data contract for your top agent input. Validate it at run start.

title: Fewer tools usually beat a bigger toolbox
excerpt: Every extra tool is another way to wander. Start narrow; add tools when traces demand them.
angles: List the minimum tools for the success metric
Remove tools unused in the last 50 successful runs
Prefer one sharp tool over three vague ones
try_this: Audit tool usage for one agent. Delete anything unused in successful runs last month.

title: Personalize with consent and an off switch
excerpt: Remembered preferences help until they feel creepy. Make memory visible, editable, and optional.
angles: Show users what you stored about them
Default to session memory unless they opt in
Never personalize safety-critical advice from weak signals
try_this: Add a “what we remember” panel for one flow, with clear delete and opt-out.

title: Not every agent should run in real time
excerpt: Some jobs want a chat. Others want a nightly batch with a morning brief. Match the loop to the urgency.
angles: Classify jobs by urgency and reversibility
Batch expensive enrichment overnight
Keep humans in the morning review, not in the hot path
try_this: Move one non-urgent agent job to a scheduled batch and measure cost and complaint rate.

title: Generated code still needs CI, not vibes
excerpt: If an agent writes code, treat it like a junior PR: tests, lint, and a human on risky paths.
angles: Require tests to pass before merge
Scope write access to a sandbox branch
Ban direct production deploys from the agent
try_this: If you have a coding agent, force all changes through CI + PR. Remove any path that skips it.

title: Give your product one voice—and make the agent speak it
excerpt: Inconsistent tone destroys trust faster than a wrong fact. Encode brand voice as a checkable contract.
angles: Document do/don’t examples for tone
Score drafts against the voice contract in evals
Separate facts from tone edits in the pipeline
try_this: Write ten do/don’t sentence pairs for your brand. Add them as a lightweight tone eval.

title: Write an incident runbook before the agent pages you
excerpt: 3 a.m. is a bad time to invent a disable procedure. Pre-write how to pause, drain, and explain.
angles: Document pause, drain, and rollback steps
Define customer messaging templates
Capture postmortems into eval fixtures
try_this: Draft a one-page runbook: how to disable the agent, what users see, who to notify.

title: Test agents with synthetic users that try to break them
excerpt: Friendly demos hide adversarial prompts and edge cases. Build synthetic users that push the seams.
angles: Include jailbreak-ish and confused-user personas
Score policy adherence separately from helpfulness
Refresh personas when new abuse shows up
try_this: Add five adversarial synthetic users to nightly evals. Fail the build on policy regressions.

title: Ship AI behind flags you can flip in one minute
excerpt: Gradual rollout is not optional when the failure mode is confident nonsense. Flags beat hope.
angles: Percentage rollouts with kill switches
Cohort by risk, not only by geography
Monitor success metric during the ramp
try_this: Put your newest AI path behind a flag. Practice flipping it off in staging today.

title: Write docs your agents can actually retrieve
excerpt: Human-only wikis with ambiguous titles starve retrieval. Structure docs for both people and tools.
angles: One topic per page with explicit titles
Stable IDs for procedures
Keep examples next to rules
try_this: Rewrite one critical runbook with a clear title, steps, and examples. Re-test retrieval hit rate.
